timeline.public-api.surface.rationale: Timeline public exports remain consumable by the route surface.

timeline.strip.math.rationale: Range URL transitions preserve server-owned millisecond bounds.

timeline.shared.presentation.rationale: Shared event markers retain their semantic presentation.

timeline.filters.url.rationale: Toolbar filters serialize canonically and restore with browser history.

timeline.lanes.presentation.rationale: Lane grouping and order are rendered from the authorized projection.

timeline.live.stream.rationale: Live frame merging preserves bounded snapshot identity and ordering.

timeline.list.detail.rationale: List events open the detail sheet without losing selected-event URL state.

timeline.strip.controls.rationale: Range picker, lens controls, keyboard navigation, and reduced motion are exercised at the route surface.

timeline.swimlanes.grouping.rationale: Swimlane grouping, sorting, and pin affordances remain capability-gated.

timeline.toolbar.controls.rationale: Toolbar controls expose only server-described choices and preserve focus behavior.

timeline.toolbar.state.rationale: Activity and problem projections map to stable URL filter state.

timeline.adapter.source.rationale: The adapter maps authenticated snapshot, overview, and stream contracts without source-runtime imports.

timeline.local-scrubber.rationale: Local source selection remains route-capability gated.

timeline.retained-overview.rationale: Retained overview buckets and coverage are created from an authorized server aggregation.

timeline.view.integration.rationale: Timeline view controls compose through the product surface rather than the upstream runtime.

timeline.url.history.rationale: Back, forward, replace-history, and deep-link state use one URL state model.

timeline.source-context.rationale: Source selection and transport composition remain isolated in the product adapter.

timeline.source-contract.rationale: HTTP capability, snapshot, overview, and stream request shapes are validated at the product boundary.

api.client.transport.rationale: The shared browser transport enforces credentials, CSRF, typed errors, strict response validation, abort propagation, and streaming media types without domain-specific fetch wrappers.

commands.cronjob.provider-gate.rationale: CronJob trigger, suspend, and resume remain absent until an exact server capability can hand off an audited CommandReceipt and durable OperationEvent stream.

helm.upgrade.provider-gate.rationale: Helm upgrade controls remain hidden while the Python provider has no validated values payload, write capability, command receipt, or resumable progress stream.

helm.rollback.provider-gate.rationale: Helm rollback remains hidden until an exact release revision capability can issue a command receipt.

helm.uninstall.provider-gate.rationale: Helm uninstall remains hidden until an exact release capability, confirmation, executor, and audit stream exist.

gitops.release-run.rollback.rationale: Rollback uses the canonical authorized release-run transition and preserves policy and audit evidence.

gitops.release-run.cancel.rationale: Terminate intent maps to the canonical release-run cancellation transition with its dedicated permission.

gitops.release-run.pause-resume.rationale: Pause and resume reuse one state-validated audited release-run transition boundary.

events.timeline.resume.rationale: Timeline reconnect resumes only from an opaque authorization-bound durable cursor.

events.operation.resume.rationale: Command operation reconnect resumes from the last durable contiguous sequence.

resources.workload.rollback-history.rationale: Workload revision history remains bounded to one exact snapshot, owner UID, and complete observed revision set.

resources.workload.rollback-cas.rationale: The selected revision, server diff, one confirmation, idempotency key, and exact CAS evidence remain one action handoff.

events.topology.resync.rationale: Topology sequence loss requests a full typed resynchronization instead of merging an unknown gap.

applications.catalog.batch-runtime.rationale: Catalog cards and table rows must render batch runtime, retained run outcome, and deterministic attention ordering from a typed product projection.

applications.catalog.delivery-status.rationale: The adapter must keep runtime readiness and deployment-source delivery state distinct instead of deriving either in the browser.

applications.detail.scope-tabs.rationale: Application, workload, and detail-tab URL state must round-trip through one route controller without mounting the wrong scope.

applications.detail.overview-projection.rationale: The Python response schema must make source, workload, batch, relationship, and completeness evidence explicit before the overview can render it.

applications.detail.topology.rationale: Authorized application topology, workload focus, resource navigation, and source-inventory differences require route-level interaction coverage.

applications.detail.history.rationale: Authorized application history must preserve partial-source evidence, deployment anchors, incidents, and source links without exposing provider payloads.

applications.detail.identity-switcher.rationale: Environment-instance switching, popover dismissal, focus, and reduced-motion behavior must be exercised in the product route.

applications.detail.parity.rationale: The existing generic five-tab detail test is expanded into application-detail parity coverage only after its typed projection exists.

applications.public-api.rationale: The route-level application tab and workload-scope contract remains consumable without importing the isolated upstream component barrel.

applications.refresh.cadence.rationale: The visible catalog and detail must refresh on the shared sixty-second cadence, pause while hidden, retain last-success data, and resume without duplicating an active request.

home.load-state.contract.rationale: Home must distinguish pending, partial, disconnected, and forbidden cluster evidence without converting an incomplete section into a completed dashboard.

home.deferred-ready.authorized-refetch.rationale: Deferred readiness must resume an authorization-bound durable snapshot cursor, use the server reconnect budget, refresh only the active Home scope, and retain the last successful projection after a background failure.

home.issue-timing.disclosure.rationale: Home issue timing remains unavailable until a server-owned event-time projection can distinguish creation-time failure from a verified healthy regression.

home.optional-capabilities.contract-gate.rationale: Home must not advertise source-only cost or MCP capabilities until an authorized product contract and provider-backed observation exist.

issues.diagnose.workflow.rationale: Issue investigation must reuse the authorized RCA evidence, report, recovery, audit, and command receipt flow rather than starting an untracked browser-local diagnosis.

gitops.detail.operation-gate.rationale: The provider-neutral detail surface renders server-observed operation gating and refresh/sync capability reasons without creating a browser command.

gitops.detail.revision-meta.rationale: The detail surface renders only the server-projected source revision; author and signature evidence remain a later provider integration.

gitops.graph-filter.input.rationale: Topology resource filtering must use the shared accessible input boundary and preserve the controlled query across graph updates.

gitops.list.operation-gate.rationale: Fleet row actions must make the operation-in-progress reason visible and must not submit a second conflicting Argo sync.

gitops.list.search-input.rationale: GitOps list search must remain a controlled, keyboard-accessible query without duplicating raw input behavior.

gitops.list.status-normalization.rationale: Provider status aliases and authorized deployment search fields must normalize deterministically without treating an unknown controller value as healthy.

gitops.list.labels-input.rationale: Label search and AND-selection must preserve focus, outside dismissal, and the server-authorized row set.

gitops.managed-resources.disclosure.rationale: Managed-resource and kind disclosures must retain lazy content, resource navigation, and reduced-motion-safe state changes.

gitops.sync-countdown.duration.rationale: A controller-provided duration and observed timestamp must produce a safe countdown without browser-derived controller state.

gitops.sync-options.payload.rationale: Application and resource sync payloads must preserve selective-sync safety invariants and typed command identity at the adapter boundary.

gitops.sync-options.validation.rationale: Selective dry-run state, validation reset, operation gating, and outcome disclosure must be exercised through the product route.

gitops.sync-options.feedback.rationale: Dry-run success, failure, inconclusive, and redacted diagnostic feedback must be rendered from a typed server result.

gitops.insights.resource-diff.rationale: A revision-bound desired-versus-live diff must handle loading, redaction, errors, fullscreen dismissal, and no-change evidence.

gitops.insights.resource-filters.rationale: Resources search, OR facets, all-versus-declared inventory, apply order, and status sorting require route-level projection coverage.

gitops.insights.focus-disclosure.rationale: Issue-to-resource focus must clear incompatible local filters, scroll once, expand diagnostics, and respect reduced-motion preference.

gitops.insights.resource-actions.rationale: Resource open, missing-source navigation, selective sync eligibility, and inline drift/event disclosure must be capability-gated by the projection.

gitops.insights.availability.rationale: Application detail renders revision-bound comparison availability and an explicit unavailable reason without inventing a resource diff.

gitops.insights.helpers.rationale: Typed resource search, facet predicates, eligibility, and severity ordering must be deterministic outside rendering.

gitops.insights.status-summary.rationale: A synchronized but degraded resource must remain visible as degraded in the GitOps summary projection.

gitops.insights.disclosure-motion.rationale: Historical issue, raw-error, compact issue, and resource disclosures must retain semantic expanded state with reduced-motion-safe transitions.

gitops.tree.icon-and-portal.rationale: Topology node icons must use the shared resource registry and never make the root resource a recursive detail portal.

gitops.provider-assets.provenance.rationale: The product-owned provider asset registry and copied bytes remain pinned to immutable upstream source hashes without importing the isolated source runtime.

build.entrypoint.baseline.rationale: The standalone product package and document root retain an explicit compatibility baseline without importing or publishing the isolated upstream runtime.

helm.release-list.scope.rationale: The scoped release list must show only inventory-observed Helm storage metadata and must disclose incomplete label coverage.

helm.release-detail.availability.rationale: Release detail must keep history metadata separate from unavailable manifest, values, owned-resource, and command integrations.

helm.release-contract.rationale: The Python HTTP boundary must apply workspace and inventory-read scope before emitting any storage metadata.

helm.chart-catalog.input-policy.rationale: Chart and repository search must use the identifier-safe shared input while remaining unavailable until typed repository and chart providers exist.

helm.install-wizard.input-policy.rationale: Release and namespace identifiers must preserve exact Kubernetes spelling through the shared input before an install request can be accepted.

helm.install-wizard.provider-gate.rationale: The only current Helm install path must remain the server-owned catalog recipe with RBAC, idempotency, agent capability, and OperationEvent handoff; arbitrary chart installs stay unavailable.

helm.diff.shared-classifier.rationale: Every unified-diff surface must classify file headers, hunks, additions, and removals through one reusable product primitive.

helm.compare.provider-gate.rationale: Revision comparison restores exact URL-bound revisions and resumes the existing audited operation without enqueueing a duplicate provider read.

helm.source-tracking.provider-gate.rationale: OCI source guidance and mutation controls must not appear before a workspace-scoped Python repository validates, stores, and audits chart-source prefixes.

helm.values-preview.dialog-safety.rationale: A future values preview must use the shared portal, focus, Escape, pending, custom-label, and confirmation safety boundary.

traffic.overview.unavailable.rationale: The route must show authorized scope freshness and explicit collector absence; it must never turn unavailable traffic evidence into zero counts or an empty graph.

traffic.overview.contract.rationale: The Python boundary must apply workspace and inventory-read scope to the normalized overview and keep unavailable flow fields null.

traffic.filters.collector-gate.rationale: Namespace, protocol, and status flow filters remain unavailable until collector-backed flow records and filter facets are specified by the server.

cost.overview.unavailable.rationale: The Cost surface must disclose authorized scope and collector absence without rendering a currency, zero amount, projection, or recommendation.

cost.overview.contract.rationale: The Python boundary applies workspace and inventory-read scope and keeps every monetary field null until a provider-backed observation exists.

cost.nodes.contract.rationale: The bounded Python node page preserves provider-neutral identity, capacity, measured usage, pricing provenance, completeness, and explicit unavailable monetary fields without deriving prices.

cost.nodes.scope-pagination.rationale: The normalized node endpoint enforces workspace, cluster, and namespace authorization, one bulk metric read, a signed cursor, and the server-owned 120-second refresh policy.

cost.nodes.observed-or-unavailable.rationale: The Cost surface renders observed node identity, capacity, and use while disclosing missing pricing evidence instead of showing a hardcoded or inferred amount.

cost.trend.contract.rationale: Trend windows, integer micro-unit rates, series count, point count, and timestamp ordering are bounded by the Python contract before browser delivery.

cost.trend.surface.rationale: The cost chart renders only observed server series, keeps unavailable evidence empty, supports keyboard range selection, and does not depend on animation.

cost.trend.projection.rationale: The memoized browser projection keeps bounded timestamps, explicit gaps, and integer micro-unit conversion without mutating observations.

cost.tabs.keyboard.rationale: Only product-supported cost views are exposed with roving keyboard selection and URL-owned state.

cost.tabs.url.rationale: Cost view and trend-range state round-trip through the shared URL codec without dropping cluster, namespace, or other product filters.

cost.cloud-console.allowlist.rationale: External console links require typed provider identity and an allow-listed HTTPS host; ambiguous and hostile identities fail closed.

cost.application.collector-gate.rationale: Application cost remains explicitly unavailable until the Python contract exposes authorized workload allocation observations.

cost.workload.contract.rationale: Workload allocation uses bounded integer micro-units, ISO currency, server-provided daily and monthly projections, paired usage windows, and an explicit unavailable union.

cost.workload.kind.rationale: The Python application response permits observed workload cost only for server-supported workload resource kinds and exact authorized workload identity.

cost.workload.format.rationale: Cost formatting consumes integer micro-units and response currency without assuming dollars or extrapolating another time period in the browser.

cost.workload.allocation.rationale: The current allocation panel distinguishes observed zero, no allocation, and unavailable use while rendering only server-provided rates and projections.

cost.workload.surface.rationale: The workload-scoped Cost tab renders the typed observed union and preserves explicit collector absence without exposing internal reason codes or fabricated zero amounts.

cost.workload.adapter.rationale: The product adapter maps workload allocation micro-units, response currency, bounded trend, and reason codes without deriving period totals or mutating endpoint evidence.

cost.workload.collector-gate.rationale: The workload Cost panel remains safely unavailable until the application projection receives a persisted provider-backed allocation observation.

topology.graph.contract.rationale: The Python topology boundary must keep the authorized cluster scope, graph evidence, unavailable projection, and server refresh policy explicit.

topology.graph.surface.rationale: The resource relationship surface must render only the authorized evidence graph and disclose partial or unavailable results.

topology.graph.freshness.rationale: The relationship frame must use the server-provided refresh interval and retain the last verified graph during a refresh.

topology.controls.scope.rationale: Topology view, grouping, and visibility controls require route-level scope, focus, keyboard, and reduced-motion coverage before they can be claimed.

topology.search.scope.rationale: Topology search must prove selected-resource navigation and keyboard dismissal against the current authorized graph scope.

topology.kind-icon.registry.rationale: Every observed resource kind must resolve through one product-owned icon registry, including workflow and monitoring CRDs, with a deterministic unknown-kind fallback.

topology.workflow-card.contract.rationale: Workflow entrypoint, template count, endpoint count, and grouped-card subtitle evidence require typed Python fields before a browser presentation can consume them.

topology.public-composition.rationale: Topology chrome remains reachable through the product route composition without importing the isolated source package barrel or runtime.

topology.breadcrumb.keyboard.rationale: The topology scope breadcrumb must expose the current location and preserve keyboard navigation to every broader scope.

topology.overlay.composition.rationale: Canvas overlays must stack in one pointer-safe shared bar, remain keyboard interactive, and remove entrance motion when reduced motion is requested.

design.warning-foreground.token.rationale: Warning text must resolve through one semantic light/dark token and one Tailwind theme alias, not page-local hue classes.

design.warning-foreground.badge.rationale: The shared warning badge must consume semantic foreground, surface, and border tokens so every future feature reuses the same state treatment.

design.sheet.drawer-shadow.boundary.rationale: The four-direction product Sheet owns its tested overlay, focus, motion, and elevation boundary; a one-direction upstream drawer shadow cannot be substituted silently.

design.resource-kind.palette.rationale: The product Badge deliberately exposes typed semantic variants only; resource-kind palette support needs a server-described resource presentation contract before it can be added.

shared-ui.collapse.disclosure.rationale: A controlled disclosure must preserve lazy mounting while keeping retained closed controls out of focus and accessibility traversal, including when reduced motion is requested.

shared-ui.multi-select.controlled.rationale: The reusable picker must filter only its controlled item list, apply bulk changes only to visible values, and leave all displayed strings to the owner-provided labels.

shared-ui.select-menu.dismissal.rationale: The shared select must preserve selection, keyboard Escape, outside-pointer dismissal, focus restoration, and a reduced-motion-safe open indicator.

shared-ui.confirmation-dialog.safety.rationale: The shared confirmation dialog must make owner-provided validation and pending state authoritative before an action can run or a modal can be dismissed.

shared-ui.dialog.nested-escape.rationale: Nested modal Escape handling must close only the topmost dialog and preserve the parent dialog's focus and interaction boundary.

shared-ui.pane-loader.geometry.rationale: A pane-local loading status must keep its decorative spinner centered while owner-provided title and detail occupy a stable bounded label area below it.

helm.release-list.search-shortcut.rationale: The route-owned release-list shortcut must focus the shared typed input without stealing an editable, modal, or already-handled key event.

shared-ui.input.identifier-policy.rationale: The common input must disable browser text mutation for Kubernetes identifiers while retaining an explicit caller override and a typed native ref boundary.

shared-ui.search-pill.input-policy.rationale: Structured search filters must consume the product-owned identifier-safe input primitive instead of restoring a raw browser input.

shared-ui.search-box.lifecycle.rationale: A future collapsible search owner must retain its externally owned focus, duplicate-registration, and blur lifecycle contract.

shared-ui.code-viewer.search.rationale: A future safe code-viewer projection must test find-state, keyboard ownership, and identifier-safe search input against an authorized manifest source.

shared-ui.resource-bar.capacity.rationale: A future utilization bar must test server-observed used, allocatable, marker, and severity data without treating a percentage alone as capacity evidence.

logs.stream.clean-end.adapter.rationale: The authenticated SSE adapter must preserve a typed clean-end reason through the product-owned log stream boundary.

logs.stream.terminal-state.rationale: A clean terminal event must retain discovered workload pods, end the matching tab, and suppress a false retry affordance.

logs.viewer.shared-input.rationale: Log search must consume the reusable accessible input primitive rather than maintaining a second raw input implementation.

logs.viewer.empty-diagnostic.rationale: A future empty-log diagnostic must be a typed, redacted server projection; the tab test will cover its unavailable and rendered states.

logs.workload.empty-diagnostic.rationale: A future workload-empty diagnostic must retain stream identity and be rendered only from an authenticated typed endpoint event.

compare.picker.keyboard.rationale: The compare candidate picker must retain canonical URL replacement, server-authorized candidates, partial inventory evidence, and IME-safe keyboard selection.

resources.physical-topology.stream-lifec.rationale: The typed physical-topology stream must expose connecting before its authenticated browser transport is connected and must keep its bounded delivery policy authoritative.

logs.scheduled-run.target.rationale: A future scheduled-workload log target must prove its server-authorized run identity before it opens the existing bounded log stream.

namespace.scope.rescope.rationale: The namespace-rescope controller proves authorized catalog replacement, optimistic persistence, URL state, audit identity, and incompatible stream invalidation without browser-derived scope.

shell.resource-search.identity.rationale: Global search returns one authorized, snapshot-backed ResourceRef and the browser opens that exact inventory identity.

shell.preferences.persistence.rationale: Theme and locale preferences round-trip through user-scoped PostgreSQL state with optimistic revision and immutable audit event identity.

issues.severity.server-projection.rationale: The Python queue projection must normalize only the shared typed severity policy and preserve incomplete, informational, and unknown evidence as unavailable.

issues.severity.router-contract.rationale: The additive Issues projection must keep the same authenticated cluster authorization boundary as the legacy RCA timeline while preserving the old strict response route.

issues.severity.frontend-contract.rationale: The additive browser contract must reject contradictory severity availability and leave the legacy timeline schema unchanged for rolling deployment compatibility.

issues.severity.queue-presentation.rationale: The queue must render a badge only for a server-issued tier and must not invent a severity for unavailable source evidence.

issues.severity.queue-order.rationale: The queue must prioritize verified source tiers while preserving server order within equal tiers.

issues.timing.evidence.rationale: A future onset-timing chip requires a typed, event-time Python projection that distinguishes resource creation from a verified healthy regression.

resources.provider-detail.contract.rationale: Every supported provider kind must project only bounded allow-listed fields from an exact API-group/kind observation and must never expose raw Kubernetes objects.

resources.provider-detail.transport.rationale: The browser inventory boundary must accept the typed provider discriminator and reject unknown or structurally invalid provider detail payloads.

resources.provider-detail.adapter.rationale: The product adapter must map provider facts explicitly while isolating raw summary and unknown transport fields.

resources.provider-detail.presentation.rationale: The detail panel must render observed provider fields and conditions, omit missing facts, and reuse one schema-driven presentation across AWS and Azure kinds.

resources.capi-detail.contract.rationale: Every supported Cluster API kind must use an exact API-group/kind projector, cap collections, preserve nullable observations, and exclude the raw Kubernetes object.

resources.capi-detail.adapter.rationale: The strict browser adapter must map the server-owned CAPI discriminator and explicit fields without parsing provider identities or inferring replica state.

resources.capi-detail.presentation.rationale: The reusable detail panel must render CAPI machine, replica, reference, node, and condition evidence while omitting unavailable facts.

resources.capi-cluster.secure-connect-co.rationale: A future CAPI workload-cluster connection must prove a dedicated capability, audited command receipt, exact target identity, and failure-safe progress stream.

resources.capi-cluster.kubeconfig-export.rationale: A future kubeconfig export must prove one-time encrypted delivery, secret redaction, RBAC, expiry, and audit retention without exposing credentials in inventory responses.

issues.resource.server-contract.rationale: The exact-resource Issues projection must require inventory and RCA permissions, preserve server-owned severity and onset evidence, and expose snapshot freshness.

issues.resource.query-boundary.rationale: The repository query must constrain workspace, cluster, namespace, kind, and name, remain bounded, and avoid transferring the event payload.

issues.resource.frontend-adapter.rationale: The adapter must preserve typed severity, first observation, unavailable timing basis, scope, and freshness without browser inference.

issues.resource.disclosure.rationale: Resource issue rows must be collapsed by default, use common status tokens, avoid a redundant resource subject, and disclose unavailable timing evidence.

issues.resource.public-api.rationale: The product-owned resource issue contract and adapter remain reusable without importing the isolated source barrel.

checks.shared-input.boundary.rationale: A future findings search must use the shared accessible input only after an agent-backed catalog and result projection exists.

checks.severity.evidence.rationale: Checks severity must remain unavailable until the Python collector emits a typed effective severity; the browser must not infer it from labels or counts.

shell.cluster-scope.selection.rationale: The authenticated cluster catalog, unknown selection, keyboard selection, accessible connection state, and URL-owned scope must remain deterministic.

shell.connection-retry.safety.rationale: Connection failures must expose only sanitized codes, preserve a single retry action, prevent duplicate retries, and never render raw credentials or stack traces.

shell.context-scope.preservation.rationale: Cluster rescoping must follow the authenticated server catalog and browser history without mutating local kubeconfig or discarding unrelated active sessions.

shell.bottom-dock.sessions.rationale: The dock must preserve bounded log sessions and audited operation progress across tabs, collapse state, focus restoration, and terminal outcomes.

shell.namespace-facets.search.rationale: Large namespace catalogs must use an abortable server facet query, preserve selected URL chips, and expose loading, empty, partial-count, and failure states.

shell.command-palette.keyboard.rationale: The canonical route catalog must drive command search, keyboard opening, Escape dismissal, availability disclosure, selection, and focus return.

shell.diagnostics.keyboard.rationale: Ctrl or Command plus Shift+D opens the authenticated runtime diagnostics overlay even from an editable control without inserting text or bypassing the shared dialog focus boundary.

shell.scope-shortcuts.keyboard.rationale: The n and c shortcuts open only server-authorized namespace or cluster suggestions through the shared global filter and remain disabled while an editable control owns the key.

shell.cluster-load.disclosure.rationale: Connection and inventory progress must be rendered only from server-owned stage and observation evidence, with unavailable per-kind coverage disclosed honestly.

shell.resource-navigation.contract.rationale: Resource and workload deep links must round-trip through the canonical URL codec without path heuristics or hidden browser state.

shell.external-link.policy.rationale: Desktop external navigation must accept only credential-free HTTP(S) URLs and cross the typed Tauri bridge rather than a server shell.

desktop.local-terminal.protocol.rationale: The local PTY must remain device-local, window-scoped, bounded by explicit output acknowledgements, and recover through a new session instead of replaying unsafe shell state.

applications.topology.projection.rationale: Application topology must preserve bounded server nodes, exact API identity, source evidence, edge endpoints, completeness, and partial reasons without browser graph inference.

applications.topology.generated-runtime.rationale: Generated runtime nodes and source-only inventory require a server-owned membership and collapse policy before the UI can hide or synthesize ReplicaSets and Pods.

applications.identity.projection.rationale: Application identity, environments, source provenance, instance membership, and version comparisons must remain server-owned and canonical across clusters.

applications.health.projection.rationale: Health, readiness, completeness, and source conflict must be projected from observed evidence with unavailable values preserved.

applications.batch.projection.rationale: Batch runtime status and activity must use bounded server counters and timestamps without assuming missing Jobs or CronJobs are healthy.

resources.dynamic-navigation.rationale: Dynamic and built-in Kubernetes kinds must retain exact group, version, namespace, name, and UID through list, detail, topology, and URL navigation.

timeline.hierarchy.projection.rationale: Timeline grouping, ownership, window filtering, event ordering, and resource identity must be driven by retained evidence and authorized relationship projections.

timeline.hierarchy.pins.rationale: Pinned resource and application identities must be canonical, persistent, authorization-filtered, and stable across namespace order and history navigation.

execution.catalog.contract.rationale: The Python catalog must authorize inventory separately from log evidence, keep immutable owner and run identity, and project lifecycle and next-step guidance server-side.

execution.catalog.adapter.rationale: The adapter must reject mismatched owner or lifecycle identity and consume server-owned outcomes without parsing Kubernetes names or status in the browser.

execution.catalog.presentation.rationale: The run rail, selected lifecycle, and bounded log handoff must use only server-issued immutable identities and guidance.

execution.definition.safe-contract.rationale: A future definition projection must explicitly allowlist executable shape, references, defaults, and drift evidence without exposing raw manifests or secret values.

resources.extension-detail.contract.rationale: Every supported operational CRD must use an exact API-group/kind projector or the bounded Crossplane composite matcher and expose only allow-listed typed observations after inventory RBAC.

resources.extension-detail.transport.rationale: The browser boundary must accept every declared strict resource-detail discriminator and reject unknown, malformed, secret-bearing, or raw payload additions.

resources.extension-detail.adapter.rationale: The canonical adapter maps every explicit server field without deriving provider state or parsing a stored Kubernetes object in the browser.

resources.extension-detail.presentation.rationale: One reusable localized detail surface renders typed infrastructure, autoscaling, monitoring, workflow, secret-sync, compliance, and Gateway API observations while omitting absent or protected evidence.

resources.compliance-controls.interactio.rationale: Compliance controls preserve server ordering and support accessible search, failed-only filtering, clear, and per-control disclosure without mutating source evidence.

workload.public-api.surface.rationale: The product workload route must compose one typed detail surface without importing or executing the frozen source package.

shared.public-api.surface.rationale: Shared detail primitives must remain product-owned and preserve the authenticated resource-detail interaction boundary.

utils.public-api.boundary.rationale: Canonical resource utilities must be consumed through explicit domain modules rather than a catch-all compatibility export.

ui.public-api.surface.rationale: Reusable UI primitives must retain their tested product-owned contracts without publishing the frozen package surface.

resources.extension-detail.public-bounda.rationale: The product exposes typed resource-detail discriminators through its own contract and adapter modules without importing or recreating the isolated source renderer barrel.

resources.job.runtime-semantics.rationale: Job retry defaults and live elapsed duration require an explicit server-owned schema-default and request-clock contract before the UI may present them.

rightsizing.contract.rationale: Python owns safe integer resource units, recommendation actions, impact, provenance, freshness, partial failures, RBAC, namespace scope, and the 200-workload response bound.

rightsizing.workload.rationale: Exact workload detail exposes the same observed-or-unavailable rightsizing union and never substitutes an inferred recommendation.

rightsizing.api.rationale: The explicit scan request canonicalizes namespace scope, validates the workload limit, and consumes only the strict Zod response.

rightsizing.schema.rationale: The browser boundary rejects unsafe integers, mismatched resource units, inconsistent replicas, duplicate rows, and malformed partial evidence.

rightsizing.strip.rationale: The workload surface distinguishes collector absence from observed guidance and presents server actions, signals, quantities, and provenance without recalculation.

rightsizing.model.rationale: The view model only groups server-classified rows by container and does not calculate impact, action, thresholds, or system namespaces.

rightsizing.presentation.rationale: Presentation maps server enums to localized semantic labels and formats safe integer units without deriving a recommendation.

rightsizing.scan.surface.rationale: The Cost request-guidance tab must wait for explicit user intent, preserve URL filters, render only validated server evidence, and navigate with the exact ResourceRef identity.

rightsizing.scan.lifecycle.rationale: A bounded multi-cluster scan must retain same-scope verified results through partial refresh failure and discard obsolete request generations.

diagnose.backend.contract.rationale: Exact resource identity, actor-bound deduplication, disclosure consent, command separation, and ordered replay remain strict Python contracts.

diagnose.backend.router.rationale: The authenticated gateway must re-resolve UID and API identity, enforce RBAC and consent, isolate history by actor, and resume terminal SSE contiguously.

diagnose.backend.service.rationale: Run creation and lifecycle transitions must persist before fan-out and must never manufacture a verdict when an engine is unavailable.

diagnose.backend.engine.rationale: The evidence engine must reject unsupported kinds, revalidate exact identity, and suppress late verdicts after a durable user stop.

diagnose.backend.migration.rationale: Run, replay cursor, event, consent, cascade, index, and single-head Alembic storage must remain reversible and deployment guarded.

diagnose.frontend.adapter.rationale: The browser adapter must consume server-described agent settings and map durable run and event contracts without source runtime imports.

diagnose.frontend.transport.rationale: The authenticated SSE reader must resume from Last-Event-ID, reject sequence gaps, and stop only on a durable terminal event.

diagnose.frontend.surface.rationale: Recent history, investigation selection, evidence rendering, and follow-up availability must be driven by the durable Diagnose port.

diagnose.frontend.motion.rationale: Streaming investigation entries, active reasoning, and verdict reveal must use transform-only shared tokens and become static, legible states under reduced motion.

resources.metrics.range.rationale: The resource metrics time range must round-trip through the canonical URL and drive the bounded server history request without a component-owned default.

design.severity-token.contract.rationale: Severity presentation must use shared semantic product tokens with light, dark, reduced-motion, and forced-color coverage instead of copying literal provider palette classes.

service-access.backend.contract.rationale: The gateway binds workspace, cluster RBAC, exact Service UID, TCP ports, agent availability, capacity, receipt audit IDs, and command acceptance.

service-access.agent.session.rationale: The target agent re-resolves the exact core/v1 Service, rejects identity or port drift, bounds timeout, headers and body, and honors cooperative cancellation.

service-access.frontend.adapter.rationale: The strict adapter preserves the server-issued ResourceRef, validates selected ports and paths, and keeps cancellation delivery idempotent.

service-access.frontend.surface.rationale: The resource action uses shared inputs and selectors, hands the receipt to the OperationEvent store, bounds the visible session, and renders only a manual loopback command for local forwarding.

service-access.desktop.boundary.rationale: The browser explicitly states that it does not bind a local port; an Opsia-owned forward remains blocked on a typed Tauri registry and lifecycle.

resources.kind-icons.registry.rationale: Every known Kubernetes and provider kind must resolve through one reusable icon registry while unknown CRDs retain a neutral fallback.

resources.extension-detail.redaction.rationale: Dynamic selector, tag, trigger, and rule metadata must cross the inventory boundary only through bounded allow-listed fields while secret-bearing values and unknown raw objects remain server-side.

resources.extension-detail.reference-nav.rationale: Cross-resource links require the Python inventory boundary to resolve an observed reference into an authorized exact resource type and identity before the browser may navigate.

resources.extension-detail.runtime-clock.rationale: Relative lifecycle time requires a server-owned request clock or explicit age field so the browser does not create inconsistent timestamps.

resources.prometheus-rule.search-disclos.rationale: Prometheus rule groups preserve server order while accessible search, disclosure, and long-expression expansion operate only over the bounded typed projection.

resources.security-report.contract.rationale: SBOM and vulnerability reports must cross the Python boundary through exact API-group projectors, global collection budgets, safe integer and score bounds, normalized severities, credential-free HTTP(S) links, and allow-listed fields only.

resources.security-report.interaction.rationale: The shared security-report surface must preserve server order while providing accessible disclosure, search, severity and fixability filters, tri-state sorting, bounded expansion, and the typed desktop-aware external URL bridge.

settings.access.surface.rationale: The settings route must select one authorized cluster, choose the first accessible namespace without overwriting a user selection, and render only server-owned product permission decisions.

settings.access.contract.rationale: The Python boundary must require cluster access, batch effective permission resolution, disclose unavailable Kubernetes subject rules, and never substitute the agent service account for the signed-in user.

settings.shell.navigation.rationale: Overview, access, preference, and administration sections must retain keyboard tab behavior, stable route hash state, responsive layout, and reduced-motion-safe shared primitives.

settings.preferences.controls.rationale: Theme and locale controls must reuse the global preference controllers so authenticated optimistic persistence remains owned by one shell-state port.

settings.host-config.gate.rationale: Host kubeconfig, listener, browser, MCP, and timeline mutation controls must remain explicitly unavailable until a Python-owned workspace contract replaces source runtime configuration.

settings.integrations.gate.rationale: Prometheus credentials now cross the owner-authorized Python boundary as encrypted write-only values with live probe receipts; integrations without the same typed persistence and audit semantics remain unavailable.

settings.integrations.api.rationale: The Python contract must preserve write-only credentials, exact policy revisions, transactional audit receipts, superseding probe state, and authorization boundaries.

settings.integrations.agent.rationale: The target agent must apply only the exact revision, bound retry and probe work, redact secret material, and preserve the existing metrics query registry during live provider replacement.

settings.diagnose.gate.rationale: AI investigation settings must remain server-described through the durable Diagnose port rather than copying a workstation CLI and local-storage runtime into the browser.

settings.desktop-mcp.gate.rationale: Local MCP endpoint discovery, clipboard, and port pinning remain desktop authority and require a typed Tauri lifecycle after the deferred OS stage.

settings.draft-close.gate.rationale: Save, discard, Escape, backdrop, focus restoration, and pending-close behavior require the shared confirmation boundary once an editable host configuration contract exists.

resources.catalog.count-availability.rationale: The catalog must distinguish an observed zero from an unavailable or undiscovered count and may expose only resource types authorized by the Python inventory contract.

resources.navigation.scope.rationale: Kind selection, related-resource navigation, detail tabs, full mode, and browser history must retain the exact server resource type and identity without accepting a stale request generation.

resources.detail.composition.rationale: The common resource detail surface composes only typed provider projections, exact CapabilitySet actions, authenticated streams, and URL-owned detail state.

resources.manifest.direct-apply.rationale: An exact source-bound manifest edit keeps Safe PR available, validates server-owned diff and impact, confirms once, returns a CommandReceipt, and resumes the durable OperationEvent stream without treating partial document results as success.

workload.detail.composition.rationale: The workload route must expose only sections backed by the exact authorized Python workload projection and keep unsupported topology, metrics, cost, ownership, GitOps, and Helm evidence explicitly unavailable.

workload.execution.integrations.rationale: Scheduled execution selection, lifecycle evidence, active refresh, and log handoff must use immutable server-issued run identities without client parsing or guessed ownership.
